text:
deploy-bot: Canary release started for chart=redwood-api, chart_version=2.3.7, values=prod-canary-2026-03-19.yaml, cluster=prod-us-west-2-canary

olivia: quick health check — smoke tests OK but p95 for embeddings-worker jumped ~120ms -> ~210ms on the canary pods. seeing a few 503s in the tail. tagging @mike @sara

mike: looking into logs now. `kubectl logs -l app=redwood-api -c api --since=5m` shows intermittent `context deadline exceeded` and a few 503s originating from embeddings calls. no OOMs.

sara: remind me the rollback criteria for canaries? I thought we agreed on either absolute error-rate >0.5% or p95 regression >+50ms.

olivia: correct. For this release: error-rate threshold 0.5% absolute OR p95 +50ms relative to baseline. also check CPU throttling and probe flaps.

mike: cpu across pods ~70%, no node OOMs. the spike seems correlated with model.variant=quantized-8bit change in values. @eng-ml any quick thoughts?

eng-ml: (bot) flagging model change. quantized path can cause tokenization fallback for short inputs — increases latency for small embedding requests. investigating.

devops-bot: ALERT: canary_health_check FAILED — errors=0.8%, p95 delta=+85ms. Automatic hold engaged.

olivia: Holding deploy for 30m to triage. If we can't mitigate quickly, plan is to rollback to chart_version=2.3.6 (pinned). @mike can you grab `helm get values redwood-api --revision` and `kubectl describe pod <failing-pod>` and paste snippets?

mike: pasted snippets:
```yaml
# partial helm values (relevant keys)
model:
  variant: quantized-8bit
  batchSize: 64
autoscaler:
  targetCPU: 65
```
```
# kubectl describe (readiness probe events)
Events:
  Type    Reason     Age   From               Message
  ----    ------     ----  ----               -------
  Warning Unhealthy  2m    kubelet, ip-...   Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503
```

mike: readiness probe flapping on canary replicas; requests that hit the quantized model path show increased latency.

sara: hypothesis: batchSize 64 is too large for the new quantized variant causing tail latency. Proposed hotpatch: temporarily set model.batchSize=32 and re-run helm upgrade (reuse-values) to reduce internal queuing. That will trigger rolling restarts though.

olivia: two options: 1) Hotpatch (adjust batchSize) and continue canary if metrics recover, or 2) rollback to 2.3.6 immediately. Hotpatch preferred if it’s low risk. If hotpatch causes bad restarts, we fallback to rollback.

mike: helm command I plan to run:
```bash
helm upgrade redwood-api ./charts/redwood-api --version 2.3.7 --reuse-values --set model.batchSize=32 --timeout 10m
```

sara: note: hotpatch will perform rolling restarts. if we need instant revert we have rollback steps ready. @olivia please confirm which to run.

olivia: go ahead with hotpatch. we'll watch metrics closely for 10m. if error-rate or p95 exceed thresholds again, rollback. mike, execute and report.

devops-bot: helm upgrade requested by mike at 1769954600

devops-bot: helm upgrade completed by mike in 86s — new ReplicaSet created, pods coming up

mike: new pods are healthy. p95 delta now +10ms, error-rate down to 0.2%. readiness probes stable.

olivia: good. we'll keep canary for another 15m then decide cutover. document the mitigation as a temporary change: model.batchSize reduced to 32 in canary; root-cause follow-up assigned to eng-ml.

mike: added changelog entry: "canary 2.3.7 hotpatch — reduced model.batchSize to 32 to address p95 regression caused by quantized-8bit variant (temporary). follow-up: investigate tokenization fallback and batching behavior."

devops-bot: canary promotion scheduled at 1769955521 (15m hold complete)

olivia: thanks everyone — marking this thread resolved for now. we'll file a short postmortem if we later identify a regression that requires a full rollback. :white_check_mark:
